        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talking to humans,” which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/fine-tuning-gpt-2</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/fine-tuning-gpt-2</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 19 Sep 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/emergent-tool-use</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/emergent-tool-use</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Tue, 17 Sep 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/testing-robustness</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/testing-robustness</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 22 Aug 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[GPT-2: 6-month follow-up]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-6-month-follow-up</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-6-month-follow-up</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Tue, 20 Aug 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Microsoft invests in and partners with OpenAI to support us building beneficial AGI]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We’re partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We’ll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider—so we’ll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure’s capabilities in large-scale AI systems.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/microsoft-invests-in-and-partners-with-openai</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/microsoft-invests-in-and-partners-with-openai</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Company]]></category>
            <pubDate>Mon, 22 Jul 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/cooperation-on-safety</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/cooperation-on-safety</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 10 Jul 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[MuseNet]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/musenet</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/musenet</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 25 Apr 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Generative modeling with sparse transformers]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence—whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/sparse-transformer</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/sparse-transformer</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Tue, 23 Apr 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[OpenAI Five defeats Dota 2 world champions]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind’s AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/openai-five-defeats-dota-2-world-champions</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/openai-five-defeats-dota-2-world-champions</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/energy-based-models</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/energy-based-models</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 21 Mar 2019 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

            <title><![CDATA[OpenAI Scholars 2019: Meet our Scholars]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.]]></description>

        <item>

            <description><![CDATA[We’ve created OpenAI LP, a new “capped-profit” company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Introducing Activation Atlases]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/introducing-activation-atlases</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/introducing-activation-atlases</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 06 Mar 2019 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Neural MMO: A massively multiagent game environment]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/neural-mmo</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/neural-mmo</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Mon, 04 Mar 2019 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Spinning Up in Deep RL: Workshop review]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-deep-rl-workshop-review</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-deep-rl-workshop-review</guid>

        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[AI safety needs social scientists]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/ai-safety-needs-social-scientists</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/ai-safety-needs-social-scientists</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Tue, 19 Feb 2019 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Better language models and their implications]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization—all without task-specific training.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/better-language-models</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/better-language-models</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 14 Feb 2019 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

            <description><![CDATA[Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[How AI training scales]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/how-ai-training-scales</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/how-ai-training-scales</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Fri, 14 Dec 2018 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Quantifying generalization in reinforcement learning]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent’s ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/quantifying-generalization-in-reinforcement-learning</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/quantifying-generalization-in-reinforcement-learning</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 06 Dec 2018 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Spinning Up in Deep RL]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-deep-rl</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-deep-rl</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 08 Nov 2018 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning concepts with energy functions]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-concepts-with-energy-functions</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-concepts-with-energy-functions</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 07 Nov 2018 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Reinforcement learning with prediction-based rewards]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based method for encouraging reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments through curiosity, which for the first time exceeds average human performance on Montezuma’s Revenge.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/reinforcement-learning-with-prediction-based-rewards</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/reinforcement-learning-with-prediction-based-rewards</guid>

            <pubDate>Wed, 31 Oct 2018 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning complex goals with iterated amplification]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we’ve decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-complex-goals-with-iterated-amplification</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-complex-goals-with-iterated-amplification</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Mon, 22 Oct 2018 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Glow: Better reversible generative models]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We’re releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/glow</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/glow</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Mon, 09 Jul 2018 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning Montezuma’s Revenge from a single demonstration]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma’s Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-montezumas-revenge-from-a-single-demonstration</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-montezumas-revenge-from-a-single-demonstration</guid>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Improving language understanding with unsupervised learning]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.]]></description>

            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We’re also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[AI and compute]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/ai-and-compute</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/ai-and-compute</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 16 May 2018 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Evolved Policy Gradients]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/reptile</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/reptile</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 07 Mar 2018 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Preparing for malicious uses of AI]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/preparing-for-malicious-uses-of-ai</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/preparing-for-malicious-uses-of-ai</guid>

        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Interpretable machine learning through teaching]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve designed a method that encourages AIs to teach each other with examples that also make sense to humans. Our approach automatically selects the most informative examples to teach a concept—for instance, the best images to describe the concept of dogs—and experimentally we found our approach to be effective at teaching both AIs]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/interpretable-machine-learning-through-teaching</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/interpretable-machine-learning-through-teaching</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 15 Feb 2018 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Discovering types for entity disambiguation]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve built a system for automatically figuring out which object is meant by a word by having a neural network decide if the word belongs to each of about 100 automatically-discovered “types” (non-exclusive categories).]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/discovering-types-for-entity-disambiguation</link>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Block-sparse GPU kernels]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing highly-optimized GPU kernels for an underexplored class of neural network architectures: networks with block-sparse weights. Depending on the chosen sparsity, these kernels can run orders of magnitude faster than cuBLAS or cuSPARSE. We’ve used them to attain state-of-the-art results in text sentiment analysis and generative modeling of text and images.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning a hierarchy]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve developed a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that learns high-level actions useful for solving a range of tasks, allowing fast solving of tasks requiring thousands of timesteps. Our algorithm, when applied to a set of navigation problems, discovers a set of high-level actions for walking and crawling in different directions, which enables the agent to master new navigation tasks quickly.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-a-hierarchy</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-a-hierarchy</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 26 Oct 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Generalizing from simulation]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[Our latest robotics techniques allow robot controllers, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on physical robots, to react to unplanned changes in the environment as they solve simple tasks. That is, we’ve used these techniques to build closed-loop systems rather than open-loop ones as before.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Meta-learning for wrestling]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We show that for the task of simulated robot wrestling, a meta-learning agent can learn to quickly defeat a stronger non-meta-learning agent, and also show that the meta-learning agent can adapt to physical malfunction.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/meta-learning-for-wrestling</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/meta-learning-for-wrestling</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 11 Oct 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Competitive self-play]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/competitive-self-play</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/competitive-self-play</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 11 Oct 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning to model other minds]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing an algorithm which accounts for the fact that other agents are learning too, and discovers self-interested yet collaborative strategies like tit-for-tat in the iterated prisoner’s dilemma. This algorithm, Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), is a small step towards agents that model other minds.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-to-model-other-minds</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-to-model-other-minds</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 14 Sep 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>

            <title><![CDATA[Learning with opponent-learning awareness]]></title>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-with-opponent-learning-awareness</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-with-opponent-learning-awareness</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 13 Sep 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[OpenAI Baselines: ACKTR & A2C]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing two new OpenAI Baselines implementations: ACKTR and A2C. A2C is a synchronous, deterministic variant of Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic (A3C) which we’ve found gives equal performance. ACKTR is a more sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithm than TRPO and A2C, and requires only slightly more computation than A2C per update.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/openai-baselines-acktr-a2c</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/openai-baselines-acktr-a2c</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Fri, 18 Aug 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[More on Dota 2]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/more-on-dota-2</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/more-on-dota-2</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Wed, 16 Aug 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Dota 2]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve created a bot which beats the world’s top professionals at 1v1 matches of Dota 2 under standard tournament rules. The bot learned the game from scratch by self-play, and does not use imitation learning or tree search. This is a step towards building AI systems which accomplish well-defined goals in messy, complicated situations involving real humans.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/dota-2</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/dota-2</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Fri, 11 Aug 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Gathering human feedback]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[RL-Teacher is an open-source implementation of our interface to train AIs via occasional human feedback rather than hand-crafted reward functions. The underlying technique was developed as a step towards safe AI systems, but also applies to reinforcement learning problems with rewards that are hard to specify.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/gathering-human-feedback</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/gathering-human-feedback</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 03 Aug 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Better exploration with parameter noise]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve found that adding adaptive noise to the parameters of reinforcement learning algorithms frequently boosts performance. This exploration method is simple to implement and very rarely decreases performance, so it’s worth trying on any problem.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/better-exploration-with-parameter-noise</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/better-exploration-with-parameter-noise</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 27 Jul 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Proximal Policy Optimization]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’re releasing a new class of reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which perform comparably or better than state-of-the-art approaches while being much simpler to implement and tune. PPO has become the default reinforcement learning algorithm at OpenAI because of its ease of use and good performance.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/openai-baselines-ppo</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/openai-baselines-ppo</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 20 Jul 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Robust adversarial inputs]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve created images that reliably fool neural network classifiers when viewed from varied scales and perspectives. This challenges a claim from last week that self-driving cars would be hard to trick maliciously since they capture images from multiple scales, angles, perspectives, and the like.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning from human preferences]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[One step towards building safe AI systems is to remove the need for humans to write goal functions, since using a simple proxy for a complex goal, or getting the complex goal a bit wrong, can lead to undesirable and even dangerous behavior. In collaboration with DeepMind’s safety team, we’ve developed an algorithm which can infer what humans want by being told which of two proposed behaviors is better.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-from-human-preferences</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-from-human-preferences</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Safety & Alignment]]></category>
            <pubDate>Tue, 13 Jun 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[Multiagent environments where agents compete for resources are stepping stones on the path to AGI. Multiagent environments have two useful properties: first, there is a natural curriculum—the difficulty of the environment is determined by the skill of your competitors (and if you’re competing against clones of yourself, the environment exactly matches your skill level). Second, a multiagent environment has no stable equilibrium: no matter how smart an agent is, there’s always pressure to get smarter. These environments have a very different feel from traditional environments, and it’ll take a lot more research before we become good at them.]]></description>
            <link>https://openai.com/index/learning-to-cooperate-compete-and-communicate</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://openai.com/index/learning-to-cooperate-compete-and-communicate</guid>
            <category><![CDATA[Research]]></category>
            <pubDate>Thu, 08 Jun 2017 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

            <title><![CDATA[Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to reinforcement learning]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[We’ve discovered that evolution strategies (ES), an optimization technique that’s been known for decades, rivals the performance of standard reinforcement learning (RL) techniques on modern RL benchmarks (e.g. Atari/MuJoCo), while overcoming many of RL’s inconveniences.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Attacking machine learning with adversarial examples]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[Adversarial examples are inputs to machine learning models that an attacker has intentionally designed to cause the model to make a mistake; they’re like optical illusions for machines. In this post we’ll show how adversarial examples work across different mediums, and will discuss why securing systems against them can be difficult.]]></description>
